text.p: The following are the leading stories in the local press on Tuesday.Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government has dropped a case against former head of state Kamuzu Banda over his UK bank accounts because there is nothing to be gained from it, a statement by the Attorney General said on Friday.

- Riot police fired in the air to disperse unruly football fans who pelted Botswana's national soccer team in Lilongwe on Sunday, injuring the visitor's goalkeeper, during a friendly match marking Malawi's 33rd independence day celebrations.

- Opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and Alliance For Democracy (AFORD) leaders over the weekend told supporters in northern Malawi they have decied to merge as the only way to defeat the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF)

- The ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) politicians in Nkhotakota, central Malawi, are canvassing for the closure of a private secondary school belonging to a member of an opposition party, to pave the way for another school owned by a government minster.

- Director of Public Prosecutions Kamudoni Nyasulu has declared that he has no intentions to drop charges against former President Kamuzu Banda in a master fraud case although government has abandoned proceedings against him (Banda) in an English court in London.
